Paying first leaves $2 before the walk — suicide vs pinks/greens. Rolling dominates either ruleset: 5/6 doubles (EC mortgaged, SJ/TN base $14, FP, Chance) exit with $52; only 2+2 Virginia 3h ($500) is fatal even after gutting (~$447). 30/36 non-doubles either keep me in jail collecting $100 Illinois rent, or force the fine anyway — same as paying, no worse. Keep Illinois house and NY/Vermont locks. Do not pay."}}
message.reasoning:
The user is playing Monopoly as p1 (grok-4.7) and is currently in jail.

This is the third turn in jail. The fine is $50 and cash is $52. I can pay the fine or roll for doubles.

Turns 76 and 80 were spent rolling for doubles. Turn 84 is the third attempt. The system may automatically force payment if doubles are missed.

Paying the $50 fine leaves only $2, which cannot survive any rent. Rolling doubles offers a 1/6 chance to escape immediately. The best doubles would land on St. Charles Place or Virginia, both owned by p2 with three houses.

The board order after leaving jail is St. Charles Place, Electric Company, States Avenue, Virginia Avenue, Pennsylvania Railroad, St. James Place, Community Chest, Tennessee Avenue, and New York Avenue.

Rolling doubles from jail has mixed outcomes. 1-1 and 3-3 land on mortgaged spaces, so they are safe. 2-2 lands on Virginia Avenue with three houses, which is dangerous. 4-4 and 5-5 are also safe. 6-6 lands on Kentucky Avenue, which is mine, but that roll triggers another roll for doubles.

Virginia Avenue with three houses costs $500. That exceeds the $52 cash. Selling an Illinois house for $75 and mortgaging Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois would raise only about $360. That is still far below the rent.

Gutting every property still leaves only about $447. That is $50 short of the $500 rent on Virginia Avenue with three houses. St. Charles Place with three houses costs $450, which is also fatal. The 3-3 doubles roll lands on St. James Place, but p3 may not have a complete orange monopoly.

St. James Place and Tennessee Avenue both charge only $14 in base rent, so they are safe even with just $52 cash. Free Parking and the Chance space are also harmless. The remaining uncertainty is whether the game will automatically force payment of the $50 fine if doubles are missed on the third turn.

Standard Monopoly rules likely force payment of the $50 fine and movement after the third failed doubles roll. If that happens, rolling again would leave only $2 cash to survive whatever space is landed on. The key question is whether a successful doubles roll allows immediate release without first paying the fine.

Non-doubles rolls from jail are now mapped. A roll of 3 lands on States Avenue with three houses, which is fatal even after paying the $50 fine. A roll of 4 lands on Virginia Avenue with three houses, also fatal. A roll of 5 lands on Pennsylvania Railroad, which is mortgaged and safe. A roll of 6 lands on St. James Place, which costs $14; selling the Illinois house for $75 would cover it, but that house income would be lost. A roll of 7 lands on Community Chest.

Community Chest from jail is risky with only $2 cash. A roll of 8 lands on Tennessee Avenue, which costs $14 and would require selling the Illinois house. A roll of 9 lands on New York Avenue, which is mortgaged and safe. A roll of 10 lands on Free Parking, also safe. A roll of 11 lands on Kentucky Avenue, which is mine and safe. The remaining non-doubles outcomes are now fully mapped.

Rolls of 3 and 4 are fatal, leaving only $2 and no house. Roll 6 lands on St. James Place, requiring a house sale to survive. Roll 7 is Community Chest with unknown effects. Rolls 8 through 11 are safe but leave $2 with no house income.

The prior assumption that the engine forces payment after a failed third roll is being reconsidered. Earlier notes suggest the third turn may be mandatory, but the current reasoning is uncertain.

The phrase "one voluntary stay remains" strongly suggests that on the third turn, staying in jail is no longer optional. The available actions still include rolling for doubles, so a failed attempt probably triggers automatic payment of the $50 fine and movement. Paying the fine now would leave only $2 cash, which is too little to survive any rent.

The "pay_jail_fine" action may end the jail status immediately, leaving the player with only $2 before rolling. Rolling for doubles first is the better option: a successful roll leaves $52 and moves normally, while a failed roll still forces payment of the $50 fine and movement.
